object_description: elevated upper volume carried by pavilion-like ground-floor piers
design_condition: The project links the two campus fabrics through a pavilion-like ground level, an upper body aligned with the neighboring complex, and a western pedestrian gateway, but the avenue entrance remains only a delivery access.

positive.statement: The implementation subtly links the two built fabrics through distinct ground-floor and upper-level strategies.

position.rationale: Top and elevations show distinct pavilion-like ground level beneath a repetitive elevated upper volume.

positive.statement: The project effectively connects user flows at ground level and through the gateway to the neighboring campus.

position.rationale: Western edge provides the most plausible gateway location, constrained at ground level by the elevations.

positive.statement: The project gives the pedestrian route the western gateway it currently lacks.

position.rationale: A western-edge opening is approximated from the plan and west-facing perimeter condition.

positive.statement: The building and site are conceived together so that neither interior nor exterior is treated as secondary.

position.rationale: The sampled model combines a broad building footprint with perimeter ground-level and landscape relationships.

negative.statement: The avenue entrance is only a delivery access beside technical premises, rather than an invitation to the buried auditorium level.

position.rationale: The eastern edge is assigned as the avenue-side access, at the technical ground-floor perimeter.

negative.statement: The spectacular ground-floor formalization raises questions about decor, kitsch, and its break with the ordinary pedestrian path.

position.rationale: The western ground zone is a plausible location for the formalized pedestrian-path break.

negative.statement: The thick slab device amplifies structural issues, adds cost, and introduces construction complications.

position.rationale: Repeated elevations visibly identify thick horizontal slab bands within the elevated upper body.

negative.statement: The banal mechanical floor typology does not provide the expected spatial richness for a place of learning and exchange.

position.rationale: Dense repetitive horizontal floor bands are clearly visible across the upper elevations.

negative.statement: The deep floor plan raises serious questions about natural lighting.

position.rationale: The broad plan depth and limited visible openings support a constrained interior daylight location.

negative.statement: A significant part of the program is missing, with no reception space and no toilets for the cafeteria.

position.rationale: Missing interior program is approximated within the ground-floor plan near the southern portion.

negative.statement: Long corridors and insufficient vertical distribution make user-flow management unsatisfactory.

position.rationale: Internal circulation is absent from the exterior sample, so a central-upper plan location is constrained.

negative.statement: The construction performs poorly against sustainable-development objectives because of its energy-intensive systems and limited daylight.

position.rationale: Building-wide system and envelope concerns are anchored to the deep upper volume and its repetitive elevations.

negative.statement: The exterior arrangements cut existing vegetation and are expensive by the nature of the project.

position.rationale: The southern-western perimeter is a plausible sampled surface location for exterior landscape works.

negative.statement: The cost of the work is above the average range of comparable projects.

position.rationale: Cost comparison applies globally and has no useful geometric referent.
